topic: AI loop engineering: from zero to enterprise
audience: Developers who write Python and call a web API; they build, ship and run agent loops and must pass developer interviews. No machine-learning background assumed.
outcome: Build an agent loop that stops on a checkable goal, retries safely, asks a human before risky writes, runs unattended on a schedule, survives crashes, and is traced, budgeted and governed like any production service.

running_example.name: Brightside Outfitters support desk and the pocket-cart repo
running_example.why: a refund makes approvals and idempotency real; a failing test suite gives a loop a mechanical stop check; both need no download.
running_example.evolution: desk loop with caps (chapter 1) -> retries and a checker (chapter 2) -> approvals, triggers and isolated runs (chapter 3) -> durable, traced fleet with tenants (chapter 4).

llm.why: every loop calls a real model; each call is recorded once with a key and replayed without one; at most 5 calls per lesson

parts.title: Foundations: the model call and the loop by hand

lessons.title: Why loop engineering, and what a loop is (and is not)
lessons.goal: Say what loop engineering adds to prompting and harnesses, and draw the inner and outer loop of a real agent.
concepts: Loop engineering vs prompt engineering vs context engineering vs harness engineering
When not to loop: workflow vs agent vs loop
Empirical evidence for loop engineering benefits: one workshop paper (arXiv 2608.21884) found 217 loops in 36,710 GitHub repos and no measured benefit yet

lessons.title: Your first model call: messages, usage, cost and streaming
lessons.goal: Make one model call through the course helper get_llm(), read usage and cost, and stream the answer. get_llm() sets temperature=0 for you, so this lesson never sets temperature, top_p or top_k: the newest Claude models reject them.
concepts: AREA The agent loop and tool calling (turns, tool round trip, termination, what a loop is vs a workflow)

lessons.title: The agent loop by hand: tool calls, results and stop reasons
lessons.goal: Write the model-tool-observe cycle yourself so every later lesson makes sense.
concepts: AREA The agent loop and tool calling (turns, tool round trip, termination, what a loop is vs a workflow)
under_the_hood: AREA The agent loop and tool calling (turns, tool round trip, termination, what a loop is vs a workflow)

lessons.title: Tools the model can call safely: schemas, validation, errors as observations
lessons.goal: Validate tool arguments with pydantic and return failures to the model as observations it can recover from.
concepts: Tool argument validation against a schema, errors returned as observations
under_the_hood: Tool argument validation against a schema, errors returned as observations

lessons.title: Stop reasons and budgets: caps on turns, tokens, dollars and time
lessons.goal: Stop a loop on every exit it can take, and say why caps are checked after a response.
concepts: Hard caps on turns, tokens and dollars; caps are checked after a response, so the last response can overshoot; enforced vs advisory budgets; subagent spend rolls up
AREA Goals, verifiers and stop conditions (machine-checkable goal, deterministic verifier, maker/checker, four exits: done, stuck, over budget, hand off)
under_the_hood: Hard caps on turns, tokens and dollars; caps are checked after a response, so the last response can overshoot; enforced vs advisory budgets; subagent spend rolls up

lessons.title: Knowing when the loop is stuck: repeated calls and the four exits
lessons.goal: Detect a loop that repeats itself, and choose between done, stuck, over budget and hand off.
concepts: Repeated identical tool call detection and loop-stuck handling
No-progress beyond identical calls: the same error twice, a state hash that stays flat, a verifier score that stays flat
under_the_hood: Repeated identical tool call detection and loop-stuck handling

lessons.title: Verifiers: a test is the stop signal, and a golden set checks the loop
lessons.goal: Use a mechanical verifier (pytest exit code) as the stop signal and a golden set to measure the loop.
concepts: AREA Evaluation of loops (golden sets, trajectory scoring, LLM-as-judge limits, regression gate in CI, pass^k)
AREA Goals, verifiers and stop conditions (machine-checkable goal, deterministic verifier, maker/checker, four exits: done, stuck, over budget, hand off)
under_the_hood: AREA Goals, verifiers and stop conditions (machine-checkable goal, deterministic verifier, maker/checker, four exits: done, stuck, over budget, hand off)
AREA Evaluation of loops (golden sets, trajectory scoring, LLM-as-judge limits, regression gate in CI, pass^k)

lessons.title: Checkpoint: the desk loop with caps, a verifier and a stuck detector
lessons.goal: Run the desk loop and the pocket-cart fix loop by hand, each with a mechanical stop and a budget.
concepts: AREA Goals, verifiers and stop conditions (machine-checkable goal, deterministic verifier, maker/checker, four exits: done, stuck, over budget, hand off)
lessons.example: Brightside Outfitters support desk and pocket-cart

parts.title: Control: outer loops, state, retries and review

lessons.title: Why one prompt is not enough: outer loops and fresh context per iteration
lessons.goal: Explain why real work needs an outer loop, and the four loop types Anthropic names.
concepts: Four loop types: turn-based, goal-based, time-based, proactive
AREA Outer loops and autonomous iteration (Ralph loop, /goal, Stop hook, nested outer/inner loop, fresh context per iteration)

lessons.title: Goal-based loops: a script Stop hook as the mechanical gate
lessons.goal: Gate the end of a loop with a script Stop hook that runs the verifier, and say why a model-judged goal (like /goal) is weaker. Also the Agent SDK budgets: max_turns and max_budget_usd (unlimited by default), with the Anthropic key only for the live run.
concepts: Hooks: Stop (a script that runs the verifier and blocks the finish)
Agent SDK max_turns, max_budget_usd and result subtypes (error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd)
Four loop types: turn-based, goal-based, time-based, proactive
under_the_hood: Agent SDK max_turns, max_budget_usd and result subtypes (error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd)

lessons.title: The Ralph loop: one item per iteration, fresh context, commit on green
lessons.goal: Run an outer loop that fixes one failing test per iteration and reverts when the check goes red.
concepts: AREA Outer loops and autonomous iteration (Ralph loop, /goal, Stop hook, nested outer/inner loop, fresh context per iteration)
Premature completion: model declares done too early (feature list, one feature per session)
under_the_hood: AREA Outer loops and autonomous iteration (Ralph loop, /goal, Stop hook, nested outer/inner loop, fresh context per iteration)

lessons.title: State outside the context: progress file, feature list, git and SQLite
lessons.goal: Keep loop state in files and a SQLite table so a fresh iteration knows where it is.
concepts: AREA State and memory across iterations (progress file, JSON feature list, git history, spine, checkpointer, context compaction)

lessons.title: Retries, backoff and idempotent writes
lessons.goal: Retry transient errors with backoff and jitter, and make a refund write safe to repeat.
concepts: Idempotent tool calls and resume after restart
AREA Cost, reliability and observability (token and spend budgets, retries, idempotency, durable execution, tracing, loop detection)
Provider failure: per-hop timeout, circuit breaker, model fallback
under_the_hood: Idempotent tool calls and resume after restart
AREA Cost, reliability and observability (token and spend budgets, retries, idempotency, durable execution, tracing, loop detection)

lessons.title: A separate checker: maker and checker split, and reward hacking
lessons.goal: Split a loop into a maker and a checker with fresh context, and catch an agent that edits the test instead of the code.
concepts: Maker/checker split: verifier subagent with fresh context, different model or instructions
Reward hacking in loops (agent deletes the failing test or assertion)
Block verifier gaming: verifier path read-only or a PreToolUse deny on test paths

lessons.title: Context growth: caching, clearing tool results and compaction
lessons.goal: Measure how a long loop's context grows and keep it bounded.
concepts: Context compaction and fresh-context iterations
AREA State and memory across iterations (progress file, JSON feature list, git history, spine, checkpointer, context compaction)

lessons.title: Tools, MCP, skills and hooks as the loop's controls
lessons.goal: Choose which capability a loop gets: a tool, an MCP server, a skill file or a hook.
concepts: AREA Capabilities: tools, MCP, skills, hooks, plugins
SKILL.md: encode team standards so the loop can verify itself (progressive disclosure)

lessons.title: Evals in CI: golden sets, trajectory checks and pass^k
lessons.goal: Run the golden set in CI on recorded model calls, and fail the build when reliability drops.
concepts: AREA Evaluation of loops (golden sets, trajectory scoring, LLM-as-judge limits, regression gate in CI, pass^k)
Replay recorded model calls in CI; a nightly live run through a batch API

lessons.title: Checkpoint: a Ralph loop with a checker and a CI eval gate
lessons.goal: Run the outer loop on pocket-cart with a maker/checker split and a golden-set gate that blocks a bad change, started by one run command.
concepts: AREA Outer loops and autonomous iteration (Ralph loop, /goal, Stop hook, nested outer/inner loop, fresh context per iteration)

parts.title: Production: triggers, approvals and safety for unattended loops

lessons.title: Why loops run unattended, and what goes wrong
lessons.goal: Name the failure modes of an unattended loop, and decide where a human must stay the verifier.
concepts: Comprehension debt, intent debt and cognitive surrender (human review bandwidth)
AREA Security, permissions and human oversight (permission modes, least privilege, sandbox, injection, reward hacking, approvals, comprehension debt)

lessons.title: Triggers: cron, events and heartbeats with leases
lessons.goal: Start a loop on a schedule or an event, and stop two runs from taking the same task.
concepts: AREA Triggers and scheduling (cron, /loop, event and heartbeat loops, cloud routines, GitHub Actions, proactive loops)
Heartbeat and triage inbox pattern; one worktree per finding

lessons.title: Isolation: one git worktree per run, subagents and review bandwidth
lessons.goal: Run several loop iterations in parallel without collisions, and keep the review queue short.
concepts: AREA Isolation and parallelism (git worktrees, sandboxes, subagents, orchestrator-workers, review bandwidth)

lessons.title: Human approval as a loop exit: pause, show arguments, resume
lessons.goal: Pause a loop before a refund, show the real arguments, and resume or escalate on the reviewer's answer.
concepts: Human-in-the-loop approval and escalation as a loop exit
LangGraph step cap: an explicit recursion_limit (its default of 1000 is not a cap you chose) and RemainingSteps
A coding agent that opens a PR, with a human merge gate
AREA Security, permissions and human oversight (permission modes, least privilege, sandbox, injection, reward hacking, approvals, comprehension debt)
under_the_hood: Human-in-the-loop approval and escalation as a loop exit

lessons.title: Injection and permissions: least privilege for unattended agents
lessons.goal: Show how a tool output can take over a loop, and limit each run to the tools it needs.
concepts: Prompt injection through tool output in unattended loops
AREA Capabilities: tools, MCP, skills, hooks, plugins

lessons.title: Checkpoint: a triggered loop with approvals and isolated runs
lessons.goal: Run a scheduled pocket-cart loop in separate worktrees, with an approval gate and a permission list.
concepts: AREA Production and enterprise operation (agent platform, gateway, identity, audit, rollout, governance, org-wide loops)
lessons.example: Brightside Outfitters support desk and pocket-cart

parts.title: Enterprise: durable runs, cost, operation and governance

lessons.title: Why one loop stops being enough: multi-agent cost, durability and scale
lessons.goal: Decide between one loop and several, from the token multiplier and the failure modes.
concepts: Multi-agent: when it is worth the cost, handoffs, conflicting agents
AREA Isolation and parallelism (git worktrees, sandboxes, subagents, orchestrator-workers, review bandwidth)

lessons.title: Durable resume: checkpoints, replay and the crash drill
lessons.goal: Resume a loop after a crash from its last checkpoint without repeating a side effect, and prove it with a drill.
concepts: Durable workflows for long-running agents (LangGraph checkpointer; Temporal in Go deeper)
Idempotent tool calls and resume after restart
Crash drill: kill a worker mid-iteration, the lease expires, the run resumes from its checkpoint; pass = zero duplicate refunds

lessons.title: Kill switch and lease expiry: stopping a runaway fleet
lessons.goal: Stop every run from one switch, and expire leases so a dead worker's task is taken over once.
concepts: Kill switch and lease expiry: a global stop flag, a per-run cancel and a 429 or always-failing verifier as drill inputs

lessons.title: Observability and cost: traces, loop metrics and per-run budgets
lessons.goal: Trace one loop run as a span tree (one span per iteration, attribute loop.iteration), and compute cost per success.
concepts: OpenTelemetry tracing of an agent run: span tree, one span per iteration; cost per success = spend / successes
Trace PII hygiene: no raw customer data in spans
Cost control for unattended loops: pilot on a slice, cheaper model for the checker, run no more often than the system changes

lessons.title: A loop as a service: a FastAPI run endpoint and an approval queue
lessons.goal: Serve the loop from FastAPI with a run endpoint, a queue and an approval endpoint.
concepts: AREA Production and enterprise operation (agent platform, gateway, identity, audit, rollout, governance, org-wide loops)
Queues for runs: Postgres SKIP LOCKED or Redis; the queue in this lesson is SQLite

lessons.title: A worker fleet in Docker Compose: scale, lease expiry and the drill
lessons.goal: Run docker compose up --scale worker=3, expire a worker's lease, and show which limit breaks first (the provider's requests per minute).
concepts: Scaling workers on one machine with Docker Compose; the provider rate limit (RPM/TPM) breaks first
Heartbeat and triage inbox pattern; one worktree per finding

lessons.title: Tenancy and budgets: per-tenant limits, per-run traps and gateway keys
lessons.goal: Set per-tenant budgets and per-run caps, and avoid the trap that a per-run budget is not a ceiling.
concepts: Multi-tenancy: per-tenant budgets, gateway keys and isolation
Per-run budget trap: a managed-agent max_list_cost of 2000 is about $20 per run, not a monthly ceiling

lessons.title: Identity, audit and rollout: agent identity, shadow runs, canary and rollback
lessons.goal: Give each agent an identity, write an audit trail, and roll a model or prompt change out as shadow, then 5% canary, then rollback.
concepts: Agent identity, gateway, RBAC for enterprise tool access
Rollout of a loop change: shadow, 5% canary, rollback on the golden set; one config bundle per release
Audit trail for every tool call and approval

lessons.title: Capstone: the enterprise loop, end to end
lessons.goal: Build the desk loop as a service with approvals, durable runs, an eval gate and traces, and run it end to end. Acceptance: the kill drill passes; the overshoot is shown and capped; an injected refund instruction is blocked; the eval gate fails a planted bad change.
concepts: AREA Production and enterprise operation (agent platform, gateway, identity, audit, rollout, governance, org-wide loops)
AREA Evaluation of loops (golden sets, trajectory scoring, LLM-as-judge limits, regression gate in CI, pass^k)
